Have you ever taken a pet on the plane?
I once put my dog o an table. To cut her hair. It went well.

I've flown extensively with my family (military) and we've had plenty of pets.

First dog was a huge Golden Retriever. We gave him a sedative, popped him into his big kennel, and he was rolled into the underbelly of the plane. He snoozed the whole way, and it went great every time. Ask your veterinarian for a sedative for travel, they'll be happy to give you one. In a pinch, some Benadryl will work too (for dogs), comment back with what size dog you have and I'll tell you the dosage.

Second dog was a purebred English Bulldog. This did not go well because we were flying her into Florida a lot, and the temperatures in the cargo hold were insane. We had to schedule the flight around the weather. Check your airline's regulations on dogs and heat/cold. You may have to get a specific flight time, night or day.

Third dog was a Chihuahua, and he snoozed in his carrier under the seat in front of me. Again, ask your vet for sedatives, but Benadryl works almost as good. If your pet is small, quiet, well-behaved, and doesn't shit in his carrier, it's easy to take it in the cabin.

Fourth pet was a cat, she hated every minute of it, meowed the whole way. I wish I'd given her a shot of something. Do not advise cats on planes. The cabin pressure fucks 'em up I think.

Let me know if you have any further questions!

Source: vet tech for 10 years

The stretch mark bit is exactly right. There is a layer of tissue in the dermis (under the epidermis, above the subcutaneous fat) that is made of 'dense irregular connective tissue'. It is pretty much a bunch of collagen fibers in every direction that is designed to be able to account for any stretching that one's skin might have to do so that the skin can return to it's original position. If the skin is stretched too far too quickly, then this tissue rips and can never be repaired. That is what a stretch mark is.
